title: Focus issue editorial: Numeracy, realism, and relevance in plant science
content: This focus issue is unusual, which calls for some background on what motivated it. One driver was the recent uptick in frustration with overclaiming and overselling at the interface between molecular plant science and agriculture (Khaipho-Burch et al. 2023; Giller et al. 2024). A second driver, related to the first, was the increasingly evident disconnect between metabolic engineers and synthetic biologists who think and work at DNA, protein, pathway, and cell levels and the agricultural and economic realities that plant breeders, crop physiologists, and agronomists deal with (Porter and Wollenweber 2018; Sadras et al. 2020; Hickford et al. 2024). And behind both of these drivers lies a widening erosion of confidence in science (or at least in “The Science”, i.e. manufactured scientific consensus) among social media influencers, the public, politicians, and scientists themselves (Ioannidis 2005; Goddard and Dalgleish 2023; Hagiopol and Leru 2024).
